tasks.name: collection-catalog-and-imagery
tasks.scopedGoal:
Ship a new LIMITED-EDITION SUMMER collection for Barkenciaga: the SS26 Hawaiian shirt capsule, built for desktop. This repo is a Next.js 16 (App Router, Server Actions) + Drizzle + PGlite e-commerce demo; read AGENTS.md and README.md first, and note the Next.js version has breaking changes (consult node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing route code).

Deliverables:
1) IMAGERY — Generate at least 15 distinct, high-end / high-fashion editorial product images of Hawaiian (aloha) shirts FOR DOGS. Use the GenerateImage tool (cursor namespace). Match the existing art direction: clean editorial flat-lay / product shots consistent with the .webp files already in public/products/ (e.g. couture-bow-tie.webp). Save them as web-optimized images under public/products/hawaiian/ with kebab-case slugs matching each product slug (e.g. public/products/hawaiian/palm-noir-camp-shirt.webp). If webp conversion tooling is unavailable, PNG is acceptable but keep file sizes reasonable. Each shirt must be visually distinct (different prints: palm, hibiscus, monstera, tropical toile, surf, tiki, etc.) and read as luxury fashion, not novelty.
2) CATALOG DATA — In src/db/seed-data.ts add a new SeedCollection (slug e.g. 'ss26-aloha', season 'SS26', featured true, limited-edition framing in tagline) and 15+ new SeedProduct entries for the shirts. Reuse the existing SeedProduct/SeedCollection shapes exactly. Give each product an editorial name, subtitle, description, editorialCopy, careCopy, luxury priceCents, a palette matching its print, imagePath pointing at the generated file, and a realistic set of size/color variants using the existing size union ('xs'|'s'|'m'|'l'|'xl'). Assign them to an appropriate category (reuse an existing categorySlug such as 'couture', or add a fitting one if that matches repo conventions). Ensure the seed still runs: reseed from a clean DB (delete .data/ if needed) and confirm no duplicate-slug or FK errors.
3) APP SURFACES (desktop) — Make sure the collection is presented well on desktop: it must render at /collections/ss26-aloha (the existing src/app/collections/[slug] route), products must appear on their PDPs (/p/[slug]) and in the relevant category PLP (/c/[category]), and add a prominent entry point to the collection (e.g. feature it on the home page editorial and/or add a card/flow to /showroom). Follow existing components in src/components/ (ProductTile etc.) and the design tokens in src/app/globals.css. Do not invent new brand colors.
4) Update DEMO_SCRIPTS.md with a short canned flow for demoing the new collection.

Quality bar: `pnpm build` must succeed and `pnpm lint` must pass. Verify by running `pnpm dev`, loading /collections/ss26-aloha, one PDP, and the category PLP, and confirming images resolve (HTTP 200) and layout looks editorial on a desktop viewport. Commit everything (including the generated image binaries) to your branch and push. Then open a draft PR against main via the ManagePullRequest tool with a clear description and, if possible, screenshots of the collection page and a PDP.
acceptance: At least 15 distinct high-fashion Hawaiian-shirt-for-dogs product images exist under public/products/hawaiian/ and are referenced by seed products
A new limited-edition SS26 Hawaiian SeedCollection plus 15+ SeedProduct entries are added in src/db/seed-data.ts and seed successfully from a clean DB with no duplicate-slug/FK errors
/collections/ss26-aloha renders the collection on desktop, product PDPs and the category PLP show the new shirts, and there is a prominent entry point (home editorial and/or /showroom)
pnpm build succeeds and pnpm lint passes
A draft PR is opened against main with a description and screenshots

- pnpm lint (must pass)

## Manual
- pnpm dev, then load http://localhost:3000/collections/ss26-aloha , one new PDP under /p/<slug>, and the category PLP under /c/<category>.

tasks.name: figma-presentation-screens
tasks.scopedGoal:
Produce the Figma presentation for Barkenciaga's limited-edition SS26 Hawaiian shirt collection, matching the existing design system, and document it in the repo. The live Figma file is 'Barkenciaga — AW26 Design System', key x5YmGrIcNmJdWjJ07kRrMj (https://www.figma.com/design/x5YmGrIcNmJdWjJ07kRrMj). Read figma/README.md for how screens are mirrored (Figma MCP generate_figma_design capture pipeline, per-screen node ids) and src/app/globals.css for the design tokens.

Deliverables:
1) Design at least three desktop screens for presenting/selling the collection: (a) a Collection landing/lookbook page for the SS26 Aloha capsule, (b) a category/PLP grid showing the Hawaiian shirts, and (c) a PDP for one hero shirt. Use the existing Barkenciaga tokens (bone/ink neutrals, burgundy/chartreuse brand, Cormorant Garamond display + Inter sans) — do NOT invent new brand values.
2) If the Figma MCP tools (use_figma / generate_figma_design / search_design_system) are available and authenticated in this environment, create these screens as new pages/frames in file x5YmGrIcNmJdWjJ07kRrMj and capture their node ids. Follow the figma-generate-design / figma-use skills. If Figma MCP is NOT available or not authenticated, DO NOT fail silently: instead produce a complete, build-ready spec — commit a new markdown design doc under figma/ (e.g. figma/ss26-aloha.md) describing each screen's layout, sections, components, token usage, copy, and imagery direction in enough detail that the screens can be reproduced, and clearly state in your handoff that Figma MCP auth was unavailable.
3) Update figma/README.md: add the new collection screens to the Pages/frames table (with node ids if created, or a pointer to the spec doc otherwise).

Commit your changes to your branch, push, and open a draft PR against main via the ManagePullRequest tool describing what was created in Figma (with links/node ids) and/or the spec you authored.
acceptance: At least three desktop screens (collection landing/lookbook, PLP grid, hero PDP) are designed for the SS26 Aloha collection using existing Barkenciaga tokens (no invented brand values)
